added_lemmas.statement:
Under uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign randomization, for every feasible count vector \(\mathbf n\),
\[
\mathbb E_Z\!\left(\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y\right)=\bar Y,
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}_Z\!\left(\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y\right)
=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}{N}.
\]
Consequently the design-unbiased causal estimator satisfies
\[
\mathbb E_Z\!\left(\widehat\tau\mid Y\right)=\tau,
\qquad
\Sigma_C(Y)=C\left\{
\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}{N}
\right\}C^{\mathsf T},
\]
and
\[
\rho_W(Y)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{H_{aa}S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}
-\frac1N\sum_{a,b\in\mathcal A}H_{ab}S_{ab}(Y).
\]
For fixed empirical marginals \(F\), all allocation-count terms and diagonal variances are fixed. Thus, for any \(Y,Y'\in\mathcal S_N(F)\),
\[
\rho_W(Y')-\rho_W(Y)
=-\frac2N\sum_{a<b}H_{ab}\{S_{ab}(Y')-S_{ab}(Y)\}.
\]
In particular, the completion-dependent term and its coefficient \(2/N\) do not depend on balance, exhaustive assignment, or the values of the positive arm counts.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}balanced\text{-}complete\text{-}randomization}\), as replaced by the general fixed-count design, is well defined because \(n_a\geq1\), \(n_\circ\geq0\), and
\(\sum_a n_a+n_\circ=N\). Since \(K\geq2\), feasibility implies \(N\geq2\), so \(N-1>0\). The unassigned label has no potential outcome and enters only through the support of \(Z\).

For \(a\in\mathcal A\), put \(T_{ia}=\mathbf 1(Z_i=a)\) and \(p_a=n_a/N\). Uniformity on \(\mathcal Z^{\circ}_{N,\mathbf n}\) and counting positions give
\[
\mathbb E_ZT_{ia}=p_a,
\qquad
\mathbb E_Z(T_{ia}T_{ja})=\frac{n_a(n_a-1)}{N(N-1)}\quad(i\ne j).
\]
For distinct arms \(a\ne b\), one unit cannot receive both labels, whereas two distinct units receive labels \(a,b\) with their fixed-count probability. Hence
\[
\mathbb E_Z(T_{ia}T_{ib})=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E_Z(T_{ia}T_{jb})=\frac{n_an_b}{N(N-1)}\quad(i\ne j).
\]
These identities remain valid when \(n_\circ=0\): the factorial factor for the unassigned cell cancels from the same ratios.

Write \(y_i^a=Y_i(a)-\bar Y(a)\). By the definition of \(\bar Y(a)\) and \(S(Y)\),
\[
\sum_{i=1}^Ny_i^a=0,
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^N(y_i^a)^2=(N-1)S_{aa}(Y),
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^Ny_i^ay_i^b=(N-1)S_{ab}(Y).
\]
The fixed arm count gives
\[
\widehat{\bar Y}(a)-\bar Y(a)=\frac1{n_a}\sum_{i=1}^NT_{ia}y_i^a.
\]
Its conditional design expectation is zero because \(\mathbb E_ZT_{ia}=p_a\) and \(\sum_i y_i^a=0\). Therefore \(\mathbb E_Z(\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y)=\bar Y\).

For \(i\ne j\), the indicator moments yield
\[
\operatorname{Var}_Z(T_{ia})=p_a(1-p_a),
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}_Z(T_{ia},T_{ja})=-\frac{p_a(1-p_a)}{N-1}.
\]
It follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}_Z\!\left\{\widehat{\bar Y}(a)\mid Y\right\}
&=\frac{p_a(1-p_a)}{n_a^2}
\left\{\sum_i(y_i^a)^2-\frac1{N-1}\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^ay_j^a\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^ay_j^a=-\sum_i(y_i^a)^2\), the last display equals
\[
\frac{p_a(1-p_a)N}{n_a^2(N-1)}\sum_i(y_i^a)^2
=\frac{Np_a(1-p_a)}{n_a^2}S_{aa}(Y)
=\left(\frac1{n_a}-\frac1N\right)S_{aa}(Y).
\]
Every division is valid because \(n_a\geq1\) and \(N\geq2\).

For \(a\ne b\), the same indicator moments give
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_Z(T_{ia},T_{ib})=-p_ap_b,
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}_Z(T_{ia},T_{jb})=\frac{p_ap_b}{N-1}\quad(i\ne j).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Cov}_Z\!\left\{\widehat{\bar Y}(a),\widehat{\bar Y}(b)\mid Y\right\}
&=\frac{p_ap_b}{n_an_b}
\left\{-\sum_i y_i^ay_i^b+\frac1{N-1}\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^ay_j^b\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \((\sum_i y_i^a)(\sum_j y_j^b)=0\),
\(\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^ay_j^b=-\sum_i y_i^ay_i^b\). Using \(p_ap_b=n_an_b/N^2\), the preceding covariance is
\[
-\frac{p_ap_bN}{n_an_b(N-1)}\sum_i y_i^ay_i^b
=-\frac1N S_{ab}(Y).
\]
Combining the diagonal and off-diagonal entries proves
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_Z(\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y)
=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}N.
\]

By Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}causal\text{-}contrast}\), \(\tau=C\bar Y\) is a zero-sum causal contrast. Linearity of conditional expectation gives
\(\mathbb E_Z(\widehat\tau\mid Y)=C\bar Y=\tau\), while covariance under the fixed linear map \(C\) gives the asserted expression for \(\Sigma_C(Y)\). Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}contrast\text{-}risk}\), cyclicity of trace, and \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) then imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\rho_W(Y)
&=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[H\left\{
\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}N
\right\}\right]\\
&=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{H_{aa}S_{aa}(Y)}{n_a}
-\frac1N\sum_{a,b\in\mathcal A}H_{ab}S_{ab}(Y).
\end{aligned}
\]
If \(Y,Y'\in\mathcal S_N(F)\), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}completion\text{-}class}\) makes \(S_{aa}(Y')=S_{aa}(Y)\) for every \(a\). Subtracting the two risk formulas, using symmetry of \(H\) and \(S\), proves
\[
\rho_W(Y')-\rho_W(Y)
=-\frac2N\sum_{a<b}H_{ab}\{S_{ab}(Y')-S_{ab}(Y)\}.
\]

As a smallest audit with an unassigned unit, take \(K=2\), \(N=3\), \(n_1=n_2=n_\circ=1\). The support consists of the six ordered choices of the unit in arm \(1\) and the distinct unit in arm \(2\). Direct averaging over those six assignments gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(a)\mid Y\}=\frac23S_{aa}(Y),
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(1),\widehat{\bar Y}(2)\mid Y\}=-\frac13S_{12}(Y),
\]
which is exactly the general formula. Thus the optional-remainder boundary creates no exceptional finite case.
added_lemmas.justification: This identity exposes the exact coefficients multiplying the unidentified cross-world covariances for every uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign design.
added_lemmas.gap: Existing multi-arm covariance formulas are usually presented for exhaustive fixed-count assignment; the result here includes unequal positive arm counts and an optional unassigned remainder while isolating the same completion term.
added_lemmas.consumer: It shows that the graph-Laplacian completion certificate and its exact regret coefficient are invariant to allocation imbalance and incomplete sampling.

added_lemmas.statement:
In the finite binary design of Aronow, Green, and Lee, \(N\geq4\) fixed units are first sampled uniformly without replacement with source sample size \(n_{\mathrm{AGL}}\), then exactly \(m_{\mathrm{AGL}}\) sampled units are assigned treatment, where \(m_{\mathrm{AGL}}\geq2\) and \(n_{\mathrm{AGL}}-m_{\mathrm{AGL}}\geq2\). With finite-population covariance normalized by \(N^{-1}\), their Lemma 1 gives, in the present notation with \(K=2\), \(C=(-1,1)\), and \(W=(1)\),
\[
\rho_W(Y)=\frac1{N-1}\left[
\left(\frac{N}{m_{\mathrm{AGL}}}-1\right)\sigma_{N,11}(Y)
+\left\{\frac{N}{n_{\mathrm{AGL}}-m_{\mathrm{AGL}}}-1\right\}\sigma_{N,00}(Y)
+2\sigma_{N,10}(Y)
\right].
\]

source.locator: arXiv:1405.6555v1, finite-population sample-and-assign setting and Lemma 1

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(K=2\) and relabel the two treatment arms by the source labels \(0,1\). Suppose \(N\geq4\), \(4\leq n_{\mathrm{AGL}}\leq N\), and \(2\leq m_{\mathrm{AGL}}\leq n_{\mathrm{AGL}}-2\). Choose fixed counts
\[
n_1=m_{\mathrm{AGL}},\qquad
n_0=n_{\mathrm{AGL}}-m_{\mathrm{AGL}},\qquad
n_\circ=N-n_{\mathrm{AGL}}.
\]
Then uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign randomization is exactly the two-stage oracle design of Aronow, Green, and Lee. For \(C=(-1,1)\), \(W=(1)\), and
\(\sigma_N(Y)=(N-1)S(Y)/N\), equivalently \(S(Y)=N\sigma_N(Y)/(N-1)\), the covariance formula in \(\mathrm{lem{:}fixed\text{-}count\text{-}randomization\text{-}risk}\) is term-by-term their finite oracle variance formula. Among all schedules with the two fixed empirical marginals, the common-rank schedule attains its sharp upper endpoint. This is a finite oracle equality; it does not assert the estimated-bound asymptotics used when the marginals are unknown.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
In the source's two-stage design, any ordered partition of the \(N\) units into a treated set of size \(m_{\mathrm{AGL}}\), a control set of size \(n_{\mathrm{AGL}}-m_{\mathrm{AGL}}\), and an unassigned set of size \(N-n_{\mathrm{AGL}}\) has probability
\[
\binom{N}{n_{\mathrm{AGL}}}^{-1}
\binom{n_{\mathrm{AGL}}}{m_{\mathrm{AGL}}}^{-1}
=\frac{m_{\mathrm{AGL}}!\,(n_{\mathrm{AGL}}-m_{\mathrm{AGL}})!\,(N-n_{\mathrm{AGL}})!}{N!}.
\]
The right-hand side is the reciprocal of the number of elements of
\(\mathcal Z^{\circ}_{N,\mathbf n}\) with the displayed three cell counts. Hence the two-stage law and the uniform fixed-count law coincide exactly. The stated lower bounds on the two observed arm counts make both sample means and every denominator below well defined; \(n_{\mathrm{AGL}}\leq N\) makes the unassigned remainder nonnegative.

For \(C=(-1,1)\) and \(W=(1)\), direct multiplication gives
\[
H=C^{\mathsf T}WC=
\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}fixed\text{-}count\text{-}randomization\text{-}risk}\) therefore yields
\[
\rho_W(Y)
=\left(\frac1{m_{\mathrm{AGL}}}-\frac1N\right)S_{11}(Y)
+\left\{\frac1{n_{\mathrm{AGL}}-m_{\mathrm{AGL}}}-\frac1N\right\}S_{00}(Y)
+\frac2N S_{10}(Y).
\]
By the definition \(\sigma_N(Y)=(N-1)S(Y)/N\), one has the required normalization
\[
S(Y)=\frac{N}{N-1}\sigma_N(Y).
\]
Substitution gives
\[
\rho_W(Y)=\frac1{N-1}\left[
\left(\frac{N}{m_{\mathrm{AGL}}}-1\right)\sigma_{N,11}(Y)
+\left\{\frac{N}{n_{\mathrm{AGL}}-m_{\mathrm{AGL}}}-1\right\}\sigma_{N,00}(Y)
+2\sigma_{N,10}(Y)
\right],
\]
which is exactly the formula recorded in the cited Aronow--Green--Lee lemma.

It remains to verify sharpness rather than assume it. Fix the two empirical marginals and list their centered values in nondecreasing order as
\(u_1\leq\cdots\leq u_N\) and \(v_1\leq\cdots\leq v_N\). Every completion pairs them through a permutation \(\pi\). If \(r<s\) and \(\pi(r)>\pi(s)\), replacing this inverted pair by its ordered pair changes the cross-product sum by
\[
\{u_rv_{\pi(s)}+u_sv_{\pi(r)}\}
-\{u_rv_{\pi(r)}+u_sv_{\pi(s)}\}
=(u_s-u_r)(v_{\pi(r)}-v_{\pi(s)})\geq0.
\]
Successively removing inversions proves
\(\sum_i u_iv_i\geq\sum_i u_iv_{\pi(i)}\). Thus the common-rank completion maximizes \(S_{10}(Y)\), and therefore also \(\sigma_{N,10}(Y)\). The marginal variances in the last display are fixed, while the coefficient of \(\sigma_{N,10}(Y)\) is the positive number \(2/(N-1)\). Hence common ranks attain the exact supremum over all feasible finite schedules. This proves the finite oracle endpoint. No random or estimated empirical distribution entered the argument, so no estimated-bound consistency or asymptotic normality claim follows from it.
added_lemmas.justification: This verifies that the generalized multi-arm design includes the full sampled binary oracle design, not only exhaustive balanced assignment.
added_lemmas.gap: The prior reduction covered one balanced exhaustive ray and did not display the source normalization or distinguish the finite oracle endpoint from estimated-bound asymptotics.
added_lemmas.consumer: It provides an exact cross-check against the canonical binary sharp-variance formula, including unassigned units.

proposed.name: Uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign support
proposed.construction:
Given \(\mathbf n\) with \(n_a\geq1\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}n_a\leq N\), put \(n_\circ=N-\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}n_a\) and \(\mathcal A_\circ=\mathcal A\cup\{\circ\}\), where \(\circ\notin\mathcal A\). Define
\[
\mathcal Z^{\circ}_{N,\mathbf n}
=\left\{z\in\mathcal A_\circ^N:
\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbf 1(z_i=a)=n_a\ \text{for every }a\in\mathcal A,
\quad
\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbf 1(z_i=\circ)=n_\circ
\right\}.
\]

\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbf 1(z_i=a)=n\ \text{for every }a\in\mathcal A
\right\}.
\]
This is the subdomain used by \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\) and \(\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\); it is not the general sample-and-assign space \(\mathcal Z^{\circ}_{N,\mathbf n}\).

prose_updates.tldr: Under any uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign design with arbitrary positive arm counts and an optional unassigned remainder, the common-rank potential-outcome completion is universally least favourable for the scalarized covariance loss \(\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y})\}\) if and only if \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) is a graph Laplacian. The completion-dependent term is count-invariant and retains the exact \(2/N\) regret coefficient, so the certificate needs no balance, exhaustive assignment, or divisibility condition. The full finite binary oracle design of Aronow, Green, and Lee is recovered, including unassigned units and the normalization \(S=N\sigma_N/(N-1)\); this is distinct from their estimated-bound asymptotics. The exact copositivity characterization for general nonexchangeable kernels remains on its separate balanced exhaustive subdomain, while polynomial recognition and the minimal complete witness alphabet remain open.

project_justification.gap: Aronow, Green, and Lee give the sharp binary oracle endpoint for a sampled experiment, and Zhao and Ding give multi-arm complete-randomization covariance algebra. The literature does not state the exact contrast-geometry boundary at which one common-rank completion is universally least favourable for every uniform multi-arm fixed-count sample-and-assign design, including unequal allocations and unassigned units. On the separate realizable nonexchangeable balanced-kernel domain, the remaining gap is polynomial-time recognition or a faithful hardness result, together with a minimal-alphabet separating certificate.
project_justification.niche: The object is neither a generic transport solver nor another conservative covariance estimator. It is a design-computable graph-Laplacian cone whose validity is invariant across all uniform fixed-count vectors, plus a sharper Loewner classification. The broader uniform-design theorem is kept distinct from the exact cut-copositivity representation on the balanced nonexchangeable moment polytope modulo common unit relabelling.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact arbitrary-count sample-and-assign covariance decomposition, proves that the graph-Laplacian equivalence, binary necessity witness, \(2/N\) regret identity, and Loewner boundary require neither balance nor exhaustive assignment, and recovers the full finite Aronow--Green--Lee oracle formula. The \(K=3,N=6\) calculations remain exact balanced special-case audits with \(n_a=2\) and \(n_\circ=0\). For general nonexchangeable balanced kernels, the project preserves the finite cut-copositivity characterization and exact algebraic algorithm while leaving polynomial complexity and the minimal complete alphabet as explicit residual questions.

sampling_model.design: The main cone and Loewner theorems use a uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign law: every arm count \(n_a\) is positive, \(\sum_a n_a\leq N\), and the remaining \(n_\circ=N-\sum_a n_a\) units receive an explicit unassigned label. Balance, exhaustive assignment, and divisibility of \(N\) are not required. Separately, the general nonexchangeable-kernel theorem ranges only over \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), whose support has \(n=N/K\) units per arm and no unassigned units.
sampling_model.treatment: The assignment vector \(Z\) is the sole random object. For the headline it is uniform on the stated arbitrary fixed-count support; for the separate kernel characterization it follows a known admissible balanced nonexchangeable law \(p\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every treatment arm has known positive marginal probability \(n_a/N>0\). The unassigned probability \(n_\circ/N\) may equal zero. On the balanced-kernel subdomain, every arm marginal is \(1/K\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The structural endpoint conditions on the armwise empirical marginal laws \(F\). The Aronow--Green--Lee recovery is therefore a finite oracle equality; consistency and asymptotic behavior of an endpoint estimated from observed margins are outside this theorem.

prose_updates.related_work: Aronow, Green, and Lee analyze \(N\geq4\) fixed units, a simple random sample of source size \(n_{\mathrm{AGL}}\), and exactly \(m_{\mathrm{AGL}}\geq2\) treated and \(n_{\mathrm{AGL}}-m_{\mathrm{AGL}}\geq2\) controls. The binary recovery proposition matches their finite oracle design and Lemma 1 term by term after \(S=N\sigma_N/(N-1)\), and proves the common-rank sharp endpoint; it does not claim their estimated-bound asymptotics. Imbens and Menzel use isotone completion for a least-favourable limiting experiment. Zhao and Ding supply arbitrary-contrast complete-randomization covariance algebra but do not optimize the unidentified cross-arm terms. Tchen's supermodular order is consistent with the rearrangement mechanism, while the proof here is finite. Gao, Ge, and Qian formulate general quadratic cross-world extrema as multi-marginal transport, and Brennan et al. use integer programming. The separate general-kernel theorem remains restricted to covariance tensors in the exact finite moment-polytope image of balanced assignment laws and gives a cut-copositivity characterization. Laurent and Seminaroti's Robinson--Toeplitz result does not supply the necessary-and-sufficient or polynomial recognition result sought here.
prose_updates.interpretation: For every uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign experiment, a practitioner needs only inspect the off-diagonal signs of \(C^{\mathsf T}WC\): nonpositive signs certify one-sort least-favourable completion, and any positive sign identifies two arms on which a binary reversal strictly improves the loss. This certificate and its \(2/N\) regret identity are unchanged by unequal arm sizes or unassigned units. Matrix-valued conservativeness remains much rarer and occurs only for a rescaled single pairwise contrast. Under a nonexchangeable balanced design, the analogous exact question is instead a finite family of copositivity tests after choosing a common unit order; this is decidable for exact algebraic inputs but is not yet a scalable certificate.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The graph-Laplacian certificate covers uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign laws and a prespecified scalar covariance loss \(W\); it does not cover arbitrary nonexchangeable assignment probabilities or turn the endpoint into a sharp matrix-valued bound. Except for a rescaled pairwise contrast, no common-rank completion dominates every linear combination simultaneously. The separate balanced-kernel copositivity theorem remains exhaustive but factorial or exponential in its direct enumeration, and its strict witnesses may require as many as \(N\) ordered levels per arm. It therefore does not settle polynomial-time recognition or binary-witness completeness.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The uniform fixed-count cone theorem follows from exact design inclusion-probability algebra plus a finite rearrangement proof and a contrast-geometry necessity classification; novelty lies in the count-invariant causal contrast boundary and Loewner characterization, not in a new general dependence inequality. The Aronow--Green--Lee comparison is an exact finite oracle recovery under their stated \(N,n_{\mathrm{AGL}},m_{\mathrm{AGL}}\) restrictions, not an estimated-bound asymptotic result. The six-unit propositions remain audit certificates. The nonexchangeable-kernel contribution is separately confined to balanced exhaustive laws and consists of the exact cut-copositivity equivalence and a terminating algorithm only for exact real-algebraic inputs. No algebraic enumeration is claimed for unrestricted real inputs, and no polynomial runtime, hardness classification, binary completeness, or minimal-alphabet theorem is claimed.
